data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible without smuggling in induction if rationality is redefined as 'strategic error elimination' rather than 'probabilistic truth-tracking,' but this defense costs science any claim to increasing likelihood of truth, reducing scientific progress to a non-teleological game of survival where the 'best' theory is merely the one currently best-suited to be falsified next.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the goal of science includes making reliable predictions for practical application (not just testing), then the non-inductive stance collapses because practical action inherently assumes the future resembles the past.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'severity' of a test is defined by its ability to detect falsehoods, relying on past severity to choose a theory for future action implicitly assumes the uniformity of nature regarding the theory's stability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) argument is invoked to save the preference, it fails because Popper's own formal definition of verisimilitude was proven logically untenable by Tich\u00fd and Miller, leaving the 'closer to truth' claim unsupported.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The argument reconstructs Popper's 'critical preference' as a methodological rule akin to choosing the sharpest knife for surgery: the choice is not based on the probability that the knife will cut (induction), but on the fact that its sharpness (corroboration/severity) makes it the most efficient tool for the specific goal of cutting (falsification/truth-seeking). The mechanism distinguishes between 'logical justification' (which requires induction) and 'methodological utility' (which relies on the structural property of severity). It posits that acting on the best-corroborated theory is the only rational strategy *if* the aim is to learn from mistakes quickly, even if that action provides no warrant for expecting the theory to hold tomorrow.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
